text:
# The Water Cycle

Have you ever wondered where rain comes from? The water you drink today might once have been part of a cloud, an ocean or even a dinosaur's puddle. Water moves around our planet in a big loop called the water cycle.

## Evaporation

The sun warms up oceans, lakes and rivers. When water gets warm, tiny bits of it rise into the air as an invisible gas called water vapor. This is called evaporation.

Plants help too. They let out water from their leaves, a little like sweating.

## Condensation

High in the sky, the air is cold. The water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny drops of water. Millions of these drops crowd together and make a cloud.

You can see condensation at home. When you pour a cold drink, little drops appear on the outside of the glass.

## Precipitation

When the drops in a cloud get too big and heavy, they fall to the ground. We call this precipitation. It can be rain, snow, sleet or hail.

## Collection

The water that falls collects in oceans, lakes, rivers and even under the ground. Then the sun warms it up again, and the whole cycle starts over.

## Conclusion

The water cycle never stops. Every raindrop, snowflake and puddle is part of the same amazing journey.
